turn.prompt: Summarize everything I have read about retrieval evaluation, with footnotes to the exact supporting passages.

answer.text:
Retrieval evaluation involves assessing the effectiveness of search systems by measuring how well they retrieve relevant information. The evaluation combines context precision and context recall, which are key metrics in this process. Context precision measures how much of the retrieved context is relevant, while context recall measures how much of the needed evidence was retrieved. This dual approach helps in comprehensively evaluating the performance of retrieval systems [1].

The evaluation process involves maintaining a human-labelled gold set of 40 queries. Using this set, the system reports recall@5 and precision@5, which are metrics that indicate the system's ability to retrieve relevant documents within the top 5 results. The evaluation also compares different search approaches, such as keyword, semantic, and hybrid search, using the same filters to ensure consistency in the evaluation [3].

In addition to these metrics, the evaluation includes inspecting missed relevant documents every week. This inspection helps in identifying any gaps in the retrieval process and ensures that the system is continuously improving. It is important to note that similarity scores alone do not establish relevance, and thus, human inspection is crucial for accurate evaluation [3].

The Project Orion benchmark is used to compare keyword and hybrid retrieval methods on a human-labelled evaluation set. This benchmark helps in identifying failure cases and provides insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different retrieval approaches [4]. 

Overall, the retrieval evaluation process is a comprehensive and iterative approach that combines quantitative metrics with qualitative inspections to ensure the effectiveness of search systems.
